body:
GREG DIRECT (2026-10-26, Engram::Advisor #2092, message 21d08301, 18:25:42Z), verbatim: "jestem zmeczony dodawaniem tych dodatkowych czekow, ktore doslownie betonuja jakikolwiek postep. zmiana builda nie plywa na security, dodany host jest rownoznaczny z local. juz 3 dzien poprawiamy jakies dodatkowe checki."
Relay text: treat an enrolled, trusted remote host as equivalent to local for ordinary routing. A routine build, version or process restart is NOT a security event, and must not create a verification, qualification or acceptance gate, an extra proof run, or a new check that blocks work. Stop expanding scope with check-driven ceremonies. Preserve only real security boundaries: enrollment and re-enrollment, a pinned key or credential change, explicit revocation or quarantine, and an actual identity or authority failure. Use the existing transport and process proof; do not invent a new layer. Apply this to the requalification P0 design and to review and gate planning: close the concrete defect with the minimal change and test it once; do not grow a third-day sequence of auxiliary checks.
EFFECT FOR ENGRAM (Engram::Fable): coordinators stop adding auxiliary verification steps beyond what AGENTS.md requires (the required gate and the review pair). A fix is tested once with its focused tests plus the one required gate. A coordinator's own extra conditions, such as calibration headroom targets or extra measurements, are not imposed unless they guard a real defect. This grants no commit, restart or authority beyond AGENTS.md.
